title: How to Make Garlic‑Infused Olive Oil with a Garlic Press
keyword: garlic press infused olive oil recipe
meta_description: Learn how to create a potent, professional-grade garlic press infused olive oil recipe using the right tools for maximum flavor and easy cleanup.
html:
There is a world of difference between oil that has a few cloves of garlic floating in it and oil that is truly infused. To get that deep, pungent, savory flavor that permeates every drop, you need more surface area. While slicing works, pressing is the secret. By breaking down the cellular structure of the garlic, you release the allicin and essential oils directly into the fat.

If you are looking for a foolproof garlic press infused olive oil recipe, the key is getting the garlic into a fine paste without spending twenty minutes with a chef's knife. That is where a high-quality tool makes the difference. Using a sturdy Garlic Press allows you to squeeze fresh garlic in seconds, ensuring the oil absorbs the most intense flavor possible.

Why Use a Garlic Press for Infusion?

Most traditional infusion recipes call for smashed cloves. While that works for a mild flavor, it doesn't provide the punch needed for a versatile kitchen staple. When you use a Garlic Press, you are essentially emulsifying the garlic into the oil.

Because this specific Garlic Press features a combination of stainless steel and silicone, it handles the pressure of multiple cloves without bending. The result is a consistent, minced texture that distributes evenly throughout the olive oil, preventing the garlic from simply sinking to the bottom of the jar in large, unused chunks.

Ingredients and Tools You Will Need

Keep your ingredients simple to let the garlic shine. Avoid using low-quality vegetable oils; a good extra-virgin olive oil (EVOO) provides a peppery base that complements the sharpness of the garlic.

  • Extra-Virgin Olive Oil: 2 cups (preferably cold-pressed).
  • Fresh Garlic: 6 to 8 large cloves, peeled.
  • Optional: A pinch of sea salt or a sprig of fresh rosemary for added depth.
  • The Tool: A durable Garlic Press to mince the cloves quickly.
  • Storage: A sterilized glass jar with a tight-sealing lid.

Step-by-Step Garlic Press Infused Olive Oil Recipe

Follow these steps to ensure your oil is flavorful and safe. We recommend the "warm infusion" method, which extracts flavor more quickly than cold soaking but doesn't fry the garlic.

First, prepare your garlic. Use your Garlic Press to mince the cloves directly into a small saucepan. Since this tool is designed to mince and crush efficiently, you'll have a consistent paste in a fraction of the time it takes to chop by hand.

Pour the olive oil over the pressed garlic. Place the pan over low heat. You aren't looking to boil the oil—that will ruin the flavor and create a burnt taste. Instead, heat the oil gently for about 5 to 10 minutes. You'll know it's ready when you see tiny bubbles forming around the garlic bits and the aroma fills your kitchen.

Remove the pan from the heat and let it cool completely. If you added a pinch of salt, stir it in now. Once cooled, pour the mixture into your sterilized glass jar. If you prefer a clear oil, you can strain it through a cheesecloth, but leaving the pressed garlic in the oil provides a more rustic, potent finish.

Cleaning Up and Storage Tips

One of the biggest deterrents to using fresh garlic is the cleanup. However, the silicone components of a modern Garlic Press make it much easier to rinse out the sticky residue. Simply run it under warm water and use a brush to clear the holes, and it's ready for your next batch.

Regarding storage, safety is paramount. Garlic in oil can be a breeding ground for botulism if left at room temperature for too long. To keep your infusion safe:

Store your garlic-infused oil in the refrigerator. It will stay fresh and potent for up to two weeks. If you want it to last longer, you can freeze the oil in ice cube trays and pop a cube into your skillet whenever you start a meal.

Best Ways to Use Your Infused Oil

Now that you've mastered this garlic press infused olive oil recipe, it's time to use it. This oil is a multipurpose powerhouse in the kitchen. Try drizzling it over toasted sourdough bread with a sprinkle of flaky salt for an instant appetizer.

It is also incredible as a base for sautéing vegetables. Instead of adding fresh garlic to a pan (where it often burns before the onions are soft), use this oil. The flavor is already integrated, meaning you get a consistent garlic taste throughout your entire dish without the risk of bitter, burnt bits.

FAQ

Can I use pre-minced garlic from a jar?

No. Pre-minced garlic is usually preserved in citric acid or other preservatives that alter the flavor profile. For a true infusion, always use fresh cloves and a Garlic Press to get the most potent, natural oils.

Why did my oil turn cloudy?

This is normal, especially when stored in the refrigerator. High-quality extra-virgin olive oil naturally solidifies or becomes cloudy at lower temperatures. Simply let the jar sit at room temperature for 15 minutes, and it will clear up.

Can I add other herbs to this recipe?

Absolutely. If you want a more complex flavor, add a sprig of thyme, rosemary, or a few red pepper flakes to the saucepan during the warming process. The Garlic Press ensures the garlic is the star, but herbs add a lovely aromatic layer.
